subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Coffee and the Enlightenment
description: Learn Coffee and the Enlightenment in one minute.

hook.text: Before coffee, Europe's daily drink was beer—even at breakfast. Coffee replaced alcohol-fueled thinking with sober debate.

buildup.text: Coffeehouses became 'penny universities' in 17th-century London—pay a penny for coffee and join intellectual conversation.

discovery.text: The French and American revolutions were planned in coffeehouses. Voltaire drank 50 cups a day. Diderot wrote in cafés.

twist.text: Steven Johnson argues coffee drove the Enlightenment—swapping a depressant for a stimulant changed how people thought.

climax.text: Science, finance, journalism, and democracy all advanced in spaces fueled by coffee. The Age of Reason was caffeinated.

punchline.text: From beer to coffee, from foggy to sharp. A beverage switch changed civilization.

quiz.question: Why do some historians link coffee to the Enlightenment?
options: It replaced alcohol as the daily drink, enabling sober intellectual debate

details.summary: Coffee fueled the Enlightenment by offering a stimulant that sharpened debate rather than dulled it. London's coffeehouses, called penny universities, attracted thinkers like Newton, Pepys, and Dryden. The shift from alcohol to coffee correlated with an era of unprecedented intellectual output.
details.whyItMatters: The connection between coffee and the Enlightenment suggests that what a civilization drinks can profoundly influence how that civilization thinks.
takeaways: London coffeehouses earned the nickname penny universities
Coffee replaced alcohol as the intellectual drink of choice
Major thinkers of the era gathered and debated in coffeehouses

faq.question: Why were London coffeehouses called penny universities in the 1600s?
faq.answer: For a penny admission and the price of a cup of coffee, anyone could sit and listen to experts debate science, philosophy, politics, and commerce. This made ideas accessible to people who could never afford a formal education.

faq.question: Which important British institutions were founded in coffeehouses?
faq.answer: Lloyd's of London insurance market began in Edward Lloyd's coffeehouse, the London Stock Exchange grew from Jonathan's Coffee-House, and several scientific societies held early meetings in coffeehouses before establishing separate premises.
